userStories.title: Event writer lines
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend `ThreadEventWriter` with the runner lines for doc writes, publish and discard results, and the optional `stale` flag on `session_started`.

**Motivation** — The API learns of writes, commits and stale starts only through the thread stream, so the writer must emit the new line types.

**Approach** — `ThreadEventWriter` (`apps/runner/src/thread/thread-event-writer.ts`) gains, each writing one runner line with `at` from the writer's clock after releasing held text (as `closed` does today):

- `started({ resumed, backend, skillShas, stale })` writes `stale: true` only when `stale` is `true`; otherwise the line is unchanged from B3b.
- `docWritten(path, bytes)` -> `{ type: 'write_doc', at, path, bytes }`.
- `published({ sha, paths, ignored, specPresent })` -> `{ type: 'published', at, sha, paths, ignored, specPresent }`.
- `publishFailed(reason: string)` -> `{ type: 'publish_failed', at, reason }`.
- `discarded(tipSha)` -> `{ type: 'discarded', at, tipSha }`.
- `discardFailed(reason: string)` -> `{ type: 'discard_failed', at, reason }`.

Reasons are plain strings, as `closed(reason: string)` and `failed(reason: string)` take today; the fail-reason unions document the values the runner produces. The new methods are additions; `started` without `stale` writes the same line as before. Prefer immutable construction of the line objects.

**Scope** — In: the six writer additions. Out: calling them from `ThreadJobRun` (US-006, US-007).

**Interface** — as listed in Approach.
acceptanceCriteria: started({ resumed: false, backend: { kind: 'native' }, skillShas: [], stale: true }) writes a session_started line whose stale is true
started({ resumed: false, backend: { kind: 'native' }, skillShas: [], stale: false }) writes a session_started line that has no stale key

userStories.title: write_doc tool and allowlisted untracked files
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the `write_doc` thread tool that writes allowlisted `.md` files into the worktree without committing, and make `list_files` and `search_repo` see allowlisted untracked files.

**Motivation** — Phase C's goal is that the thread ends with `.nax/features/<feature>/spec.md` in the checkout; the agent needs a safe write tool and must be able to find what it wrote.

**Approach** — `writeDocTool(ctx)` in new `apps/runner/src/thread/tools/write-doc.ts`, input `{ path: string, content: string }` (both required, `additionalProperties: false`), `approval: 'never'`. Steps, in order, the first failure returning an `isError: true` result and writing nothing:

1. `path` must pass `isAllowedThreadDocPath(path, ctx.feature ?? '')`, else `path not allowed: <path>`;
2. `content` must be a string, else `content must be a string`;
3. `content` must be at most `THREAD_DOC_LIMITS.maxFileBytes` UTF-8 bytes, else `content too large`;
4. no existing segment of `<worktree>/<path>` (each directory, then the file) may be a symlink, else `refused symlink: <relative path>`;
5. create the parent directories; the parent's real path must be inside the worktree's real path, else `path escapes the worktree`;
6. write `content` as UTF-8, replacing an existing file; return `wrote <path> (<bytes> bytes)`; then call `ctx.onDocWritten?.(path, bytes)`.

The tool's `run` goes through `refuseInvalidInput` (`tools/shared.ts`), so any filesystem error (the target is a directory, a parent segment is a regular file, no space, no permission) returns `isError: true` with the sanitized error message and calls no `onDocWritten`. Mirror `symlinkOnPath` / `applyEdits` in `apps/runner/src/executor/config-job/apply-edits.ts` for the symlink and real-path checks.

The tool never runs git: the file stays untracked or modified until Publish. The `ThreadTool` doc comment in `tools/types.ts` ("A read-only thread tool") becomes "A thread tool".

`ThreadToolContext` (`thread/tools/types.ts`) gains optional `feature?: string` (absent: only `docs/**` is allowlisted, because no `.nax/features/<feature>/` prefix can match) and `onDocWritten?: (path: string, bytes: number) => void`; optional so the existing tool-test contexts still type-check. `buildThreadTools` returns five tools, `write_doc` last.

`list_files` also lists untracked, non-ignored files (`git ls-files -z --others --exclude-standard` with the same `dir` / `glob` pathspec) that pass `isAllowedThreadDocPath(path, ctx.feature ?? '')`. The result is the tracked list followed by those untracked paths, de-duplicated in first-seen order, then cut by the same entry and byte caps.

`search_repo` runs in two steps: the existing tracked `git grep`, then, when there are allowlisted untracked paths (listed as above with the search's `glob`), a second `git grep --no-index` with the same flags limited to those literal paths. Hit lines are the tracked hits followed by the untracked ones, de-duplicated in first-seen order; the `max` and byte caps apply to the combined list. Untracked files outside the allowlist and ignored files never appear in either tool. The tool descriptions say so.

Existing tests to update: `apps/runner/test/unit/thread-skill-tools.spec.ts` line 136 (tool-name list gains `'write_doc'` last; order of the first four unchanged) and line 142 (approvals become five `'never'`); `apps/runner/test/unit/thread-tools-embedder.spec.ts` line 18 (names list gains `'write_doc'`) and line 29 (`tools.length` 4 -> 5); `apps/runner/test/unit/thread-tools-review.spec.ts` line 43 (recorded git timeouts `[4_321]` -> `[4_321, 4_321]`, because `list_files` now issues a second `ls-files` call).

**Scope** — In: `write-doc.ts`, `ThreadToolContext` fields, `buildThreadTools`, `list_files`/`search_repo` untracked handling, the listed test updates. Out: wiring `feature`/`onDocWritten` into the session (US-006); Publish (US-004).

**Interface** — `writeDocTool(ctx: ThreadToolContext): ThreadTool`; `ThreadToolContext` gains `feature?: string` and `onDocWritten?: (path: string, bytes: number) => void`.

Also: the test at line 142 asserting the approvals are exactly four `'never'` becomes five `'never'`, because this story adds `write_doc` with `approval: 'never'`.

userStories.title: ThreadJobRun live publish, write_doc lines and stale announce
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Wire `write_doc`, live-session `THREAD_PUBLISH` and the stale announce into `ThreadJobRun`, with the publish state and handlers in a new sibling module.

**Motivation** — A running brainstorm must write docs, announce them on the stream, and let the user publish them from the live session without racing turns, input or close.

**Approach** — `ThreadHostDeps` (`thread/thread-job-run.ts:60`) gains `publish?: (input: ThreadPublishInput) => Promise<ThreadPublishResult>` (default `publishThreadDocs`) and, for US-007, `discard?`. As the existing seams (`thread-job-run.ts:18-44`), `ThreadPublishInput` = `Seam<PublishThreadDocsInput>` and the result widens `reason` to `string`: `{ ok: true; sha; paths; ignored; specPresent } | { ok: false; reason: string; detail?: string }`.

- The publish-in-flight state and the `THREAD_PUBLISH` handling live in `thread/thread-live-publish.ts`; `ThreadJobRun` calls into it, so `thread-job-run.ts` (785 lines today) gains only the wiring calls.
- The tool context gets `feature: thread.feature` and `onDocWritten` that writes `writer.docWritten(path, bytes)` when the writer exists.
- `openStream` passes `stale: prepared.stale` to `writer.started`.
- `command('THREAD_PUBLISH', payload)` on a `RUNNING` session, after the existing `session_closed` / `session_not_ready` checks: a running turn -> `rejected` `turn_running`; a publish already in flight -> `rejected` `publishing`; otherwise `ok`, and the publish runs in the background through `host.publish` (default `publishThreadDocs`) with `git: host.git`, `mutex: deps.mutex`, `repoKey: row.repoKey`, the prepared worktree, `feature` and `threadId` from the ASSIGN's `thread`, `title: thread.title ?? thread.feature` and `identity: row.assign.gitIdentity`.
- While a publish is in flight the idle timer is stopped and `THREAD_INPUT` answers `rejected` `publishing`. When it settles, the writer gets `published(...)` or `publishFailed(reason)` and the idle timer is armed again.
- A close (idle, `THREAD_CLOSE`, cancel, cost or stream cap) that starts while a publish is in flight waits for it, so the result line comes before `session_closed`. After a halt nothing is written.
- `ThreadRunDeps.mutex` becomes `Pick<RepoMutex, 'acquire'> & Partial<Pick<RepoMutex, 'isLocked'>>`, so the eight existing thread-run test fixtures (`mutex: { acquire }`) still type-check. The run hands `publishThreadDocs` a mutex whose `isLocked` is `(key) => deps.mutex.isLocked(key)` when `deps.mutex.isLocked` exists (called on `deps.mutex`, so `this` stays bound) and `() => false` otherwise. Production always has it: the Supervisor passes the daemon's real `RepoMutex` (`supervisor.ts:47`).
- `ThreadJobRun.command` (`thread-job-run.ts:639`) previously rejected `THREAD_PUBLISH` as `unsupported`; routing in `CommandHandler.handle` -> `Supervisor.threadCommand` -> `ThreadJobRun.command` is unchanged. A `host.publish` that throws is treated as `{ ok: false, reason: 'git_error' }`; a `publish_failed` result leaves the row `RUNNING`.

**Scope** — In: `thread-live-publish.ts`, `thread-job-run.ts` wiring, `ThreadRunDeps.mutex` type, `host.publish` seam. Out: the PUBLISH/DISCARD job path, `host.discard` default and capability flag (US-007); the unit implementations of `write_doc`, Publish and the writer (US-002..US-004, already built).

**Interface** — see Approach.

routing.reasoning: Concurrent state in the central session class (publish in flight vs turns, input, idle timer, close ordering) but confined to one new module plus wiring calls, so no architectural change warranting strict isolation.

userStories.title: PUBLISH and DISCARD jobs and the threadWrite capability
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Run `PUBLISH` and `DISCARD` THREAD jobs without a session through a new `thread-action-run.ts`, and report `threadWrite: true` from the nax capability probe.

**Motivation** — When no session is live the API must still publish or discard a thread's files, and it must be able to tell that this runner supports the write path.

**Approach** — Rulings: C1-R2 Discard is only a `THREAD` job action (`DISCARD`) that runs when no session is live; there is no `THREAD_DISCARD` command. C1-R3 the runner advertises the write path with `threadWrite: true`; `FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays `4`. C1-D2 a `PUBLISH` or `DISCARD` job opens no session, acquires no git credentials, fetches nothing and prepares no skills. It goes `RUNNING`, writes exactly one result line to its `thread` stream (no `session_started`), drains the stream, then `UPLOADING` -> `COMPLETED` with `stateReason` equal to the result line's `type`.

- `action: 'PUBLISH'` or `'DISCARD'`: after the cancel check, no `credentials.acquire`, no `prepareWorktree`, no `ensureSkills`, no `sessions.open`. The row goes `RUNNING`, the stream file is created and registered as for a session, and no `session_started` line is written.
- `PUBLISH`: `host.publish` with the same input as US-006, `worktree: threadWorktreeDir(homeDir, threadId)`; the writer gets `published` / `publishFailed`.
- `DISCARD`: `host.discard` (default `discardThreadChanges`) with `homeDir`, `repoDir` (as `prepare` builds it), `threadId`, `feature` and `baseRef: row.assign.ref`; the writer gets `discarded(tipSha)` / `discardFailed(reason)`. `ThreadHostDeps` gains `discard?: (input: ThreadDiscardInput) => Promise<ThreadDiscardResult>`, with `ThreadDiscardInput` = `Seam<DiscardThreadChangesInput>` and result `{ ok: true; tipSha } | { ok: false; reason: string; detail?: string }`.
- Then the stream drains (as `finishRun`), `UPLOADING`, `COMPLETED` with `stateReason` the line type (`published`, `publish_failed`, `discarded`, `discard_failed`), `markDone`.
- Any thread command to a `PUBLISH` / `DISCARD` job answers `rejected` `no_session`, checked before the command switch. `requestCancel` before `RUNNING` ends it `CANCELLED` as today; once the job is `RUNNING`, `requestCancel` records `cancelRequestedAt` but does not close it: the git work finishes and the job ends with its result line and `COMPLETED`, with no `session_closed` line.
- A `host.publish` or `host.discard` that throws is treated as `{ ok: false, reason: 'git_error' }`.
- The `PUBLISH` / `DISCARD` path lives in `thread/thread-action-run.ts`, called from `ThreadJobRun.run` (`thread-job-run.ts:208`), which previously always opened a session.
- `NaxCapabilityProbe.probe` (`apps/runner/src/capabilities/nax-probe.ts`) adds `threadWrite: true` to the report it builds. `StaticCapabilityProbe` (runner.json capabilities) is unchanged and reports no `threadWrite`, as it reports no `threadBackends`.

analysis: Runner-only feature (apps/runner plus packages/fleet-protocol). No API or web changes (C1-R1); FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 4 (C1-R3). Key files: packages/fleet-protocol/src/threads.ts (ThreadAction, ThreadAssign, ThreadRunnerLine), nax-config-paths.ts (allowlist pattern to mirror), index.ts (RunnerCapabilities); apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts (parseAssign THREAD branch, line ~145); thread/thread-event-writer.ts; thread/tools/{types,index,list-files,search-repo}.ts (+ new write-doc.ts); thread/thread-worktree.ts (prepareThreadWorktree, resolveTip must be exported); thread/thread-job-run.ts (785 lines already: add only wiring calls, new logic goes in sibling modules thread-live-publish.ts and thread-action-run.ts); executor/config-job/{apply-edits,commit-push}.ts (symlink checks and explicit-identity commit to mirror); supervisor/repo-mutex.ts (acquire, isLocked); capabilities/nax-probe.ts. Dependency order: US-001 first (allowlist + protocol types used by all), then US-002..US-005 are independent of each other, US-006 integrates them into the live session, US-007 adds the PUBLISH/DISCARD job path and capability flag. Risks: (1) existing tests that assert old behaviour must be updated as listed per story (assign-parser-thread.spec.ts PUBLISH test, thread-skill-tools.spec.ts tool lists/approvals, thread-tools-embedder.spec.ts, thread-tools-review.spec.ts timeouts [4_321,4_321], thread-worktree.spec.ts worktree_conflict test, nax-probe.spec.ts capabilities object). (2) ThreadToolContext.feature/onDocWritten, ThreadPrepareResult.stale and ThreadRunDeps.mutex.isLocked must be optional so existing test fixtures still type-check. (3) list_files/search_repo gain a second git call; the thread-tools.spec.ts fake answers every ls-files call with the tracked list, so results must be de-duplicated in first-seen order. (4) Publish must never leave the repo mutex locked (finally), never wait on it (isLocked check then acquire), and must never push/fetch. (5) Publish/Discard must verify the directory is really the thread worktree (.git exists and rev-parse --show-toplevel equals realpath) so a plain directory inside another repo is never mutated. (6) createGit forces LC_ALL=C so 'would be overwritten' stderr matching is stable. (7) Immutability and small files: keep new modules focused; thread-job-run.ts must not grow beyond wiring. Build gate per story: bun run type-check and bun run lint in apps/runner; US-001 also bun run type-check at repo root. Tests are bun:test; real temporary git repos use apps/runner/test/helpers/git-fixture.ts (git, isolateGit).
outOfScope: The API side of phase C belongs to feature C2 `fleet-s5a-thread-handoff`: queueing `THREAD_PUBLISH`, creating `PUBLISH` / `DISCARD` jobs, sending `thread.title`, gating on `threadWrite`, the `writtenPaths` / `publishedSha` / `specPublished` columns, folding the `write_doc`, `published`, `publish_failed`, `discarded`, `discard_failed` lines and `session_started.stale`, the one-active-job rule, Plan and Run dispatch from a thread, the PLAN `branch_mismatch` verdict and the system-prompt text about `write_doc`.
The web side of phase C (action bar, Discard banner, commit markers, PLAN / RUN cards) belongs to feature C3.
The runner never pushes a published commit; the thread's PLAN pushes `feat/<feature>` later.
`write_doc` cannot delete or rename files and writes only `.md` files under the allowlist; there is no binary write.
There is no `THREAD_DISCARD` command and no in-session discard (C1-R2).
Publish does not wait for the repo mutex (C1-R4).
ACP backends belong to phase D; `write_doc` is a native-session tool only.
Base-ref drift is not rebased; a stale session stays on its old HEAD until Discard.
The runner `context.md` (`.nax/mono/apps/runner/context.md`) is updated by hand after merge.

A `PUBLISH` or `DISCARD` job re-adopted after a daemon restart ends `FAILED` (`a thread job cannot be resumed`), even if its commit landed; the user publishes again, which then finds nothing to commit.

US-001 only: the allowlist's backslash, NUL, empty-stem (`docs/.md`), bare `docs.md` and 512-character boundary cases, a `title` that is absent (the parsed thread has no `title` key) and `THREAD_DOC_LIMITS` itself share the rules in Design without a dedicated acceptance criterion; `ThreadRunnerLine` and the two fail-reason unions are types, checked by `bun run type-check`. A `DISCARD` ASSIGN with a non-null `initialMessage` returns `invalid initialMessage` by the same rule as `PUBLISH` (AC-12) without its own acceptance criterion.

US-003 only: the exact 524288-byte boundary, `list_files`' `dir` / `glob` filter on untracked files, an ignored file in either tool, `search_repo`'s `fixed`, `max` and timeout rules for untracked files, a `write_doc` parent that resolves outside the worktree without a symlink, a filesystem error (through `refuseInvalidInput`), the absent-`feature` context and the de-duplication of tracked and untracked results (exercised by the existing `thread-tools.spec.ts` fake, which answers every `ls-files` call with the tracked list) share the rules in Design without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-004 only: an untracked symlink or a deleted file under the allowlist (both go to `ignored`), a staged file outside `paths`, the commit's single parent and author, nothing to commit (the branch is created at HEAD when absent, `paths: []`), `specPresent: false`, a non-zero `update-ref` exit after the compare (with its `reset --soft`), the git timeout and a failing git call (`git_error` with a sanitized `detail`) share the steps in Design without a dedicated acceptance criterion; so do the `title` CR / LF replacement, the 200-character cut and the explicit identity, which follow `commitAndPushConfig`.

US-005 only: the tip-resolution fallbacks after the local branch reuse `prepareThreadWorktree`'s order, Discard makes no `fetch` call, and a failing git call during Discard is `git_error`, without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-006 only: the live-session `THREAD_PUBLISH` through the unstubbed default `publishThreadDocs` (the default is run on a real repository through the action path in US-007), a `publish_failed` result leaving the row `RUNNING`, `stale: false` writing no `stale` key (pinned on the writer in US-002), a `THREAD_PUBLISH` during a turn not calling `host.publish`, a publish settling after a halt and a `host.publish` that throws (treated as `git_error`) share the rules in Design without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-007 only: the row's `doneAt`, the stream drain before `UPLOADING` (the existing `finishRun` order), a `DISCARD` job's `discard_failed` line and stateReason, a cancel requested before `RUNNING` (the existing `stopped()` path), a throwing `host.publish` / `host.discard` (treated as `git_error`), and a halt or ABANDON while a `PUBLISH` / `DISCARD` job runs (the existing halt path: no line, no transition) share the rules in Design without a dedicated acceptance criterion.
